quest.title: The Case of the Crafting Bench
quest.description: You discover a strange Crafting Bench in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.speaker: "Crafting Bench"
dialogues.text: Water and earth, wind and fire, craft for me what ah... ATCHOO! ... I d—desire.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, is Paimon hearing things, or did that Crafting Bench just sneeze?

dialogues.speaker: "Crafting Bench"
dialogues.text: Water and earth, wind and fire, craft for me what I desire.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Back to normal now, it seems.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Err...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon thinks we're better off not using this weird Crafting Bench, {NICKNAME}...
So you won't be needing it, then? In that case, don't mind me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But this one's really odd and stuff...
What do you mean? Don't they all look like this? Don't worry, I won't be too long.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The young lady submits the materials required by the recipe, and you exchange some words while the potions are being synthesized. You learn her name, Sumac, and learn that this is her first time at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame...

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: See? Nothing wrong with it at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright. Maybe even Crafting Benches can feel under the weather sometimes?

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: That's a good one, Paimon. Saurians or humans can be off their game, sure, but a Crafting Bench is just an object.

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, speaking of which, would you two have time for a friendly sparring match? I'd like to test the potion I just made. It's said to help with "adjusting your current state."

choices.text: If it works, give me the recipe, would you?

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Haha, no problem!

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: I know a nice clearing near the Stadium. We only need to test out the potion, so it shouldn't take too much of your time. What do you say?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As long as it's quick...

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Haha! I knew you'd be up for it. Let's go, then!

choices.text: I fear the endless battles have already worn away at mine flesh and soul...

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Endless battle is a warrior's fate, and that makes it all the more paramount that we spar and hone ourselves, that we will not be defeated in our upcoming battles, no?

talks.objective: Go to the clearing near the Stadium of the Sacred Flame

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: This place ain't half bad, huh? Shall we get right to it?

choices.text: Bring it on!

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: I was waiting for you to say that.

choices.text: I'll need a moment to prepare.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: No worries. I'll wait here.

dialogues.speaker: Anela
dialogues.text: Sour Sauce Ceviche again...?

choices.text: What's wrong with Sour Sauce Ceviche?

response.speaker: Anela
response.text: Nothing, really, it's fine. But no matter how good it is, you can't just keep eating the same thing day after day, can you? Though on the other hand, Ripple's been getting a bit pudgy lately, hasn't he? Odd, neither his training nor his caloric intake have changed...

choices.text: I shan't disturb you any longer.

response.speaker: Anela
response.text: Aw, it's fine!

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Urgh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—Hey, you sure you're okay? You started acting all weird the second you ingested it...

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: It's so...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does it hurt? Stop talking for now — just get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: ...So incredibly effective... at "adjusting one's state"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Seriously!? Now's not the time for joking! C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's get her somewhere she can be treated, stat!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, how was that? Strong enough for you?

dialogues.speaker: Ogun
dialogues.text: A diamond in the rough, but a diamond nonetheless. What do you want to know?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As agreed, Ogun tells of his previous ordeal, sparing no detail. Hampeq in turn records the testimony as given.

dialogues.speaker: Ogun
dialogues.text: Pah. But what's the use of taking all this testimony? It's a waste of time.

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: He is no warrior who gives up before battle is joined. I will give it my all, regardless of what you say.

dialogues.speaker: Ogun
dialogues.text: Suit yourself, then.

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. I feel much better now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew! Paimon's glad you're okay. You scared the stuffing out of us!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It could have been a tricky misunderstanding to clear up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! Now that Paimon thinks about it... If that had been some kinda poison, we might be taken for murderers!

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Oh, it's fine. Not to brag or anything, but I've been in superb health since I was little. Why, I can count the number of times I've fallen sick on one hand. This is no biggie.

choices.text: A will of stone can shatter any obstacle!

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: You're right! That's the resolve warriors should have.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon! There are obstacles that even willpower won't let you barge through! Should you really be pushing yourself if you've been poisoned!?

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: True enough — Though I'd say the formula for the potion was fine. It certainly isn't a poison, at any rate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean you got it from a trusted source?

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: No, I bought it from a merchant named Soncoyoc. He only comes out after sunset, and it just happened to be night when I ran into him! How lucky!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lucky!? That sounds super suspicious! You totally got scammed — we've gotta find that liar, and set his pants on fire!

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: There's no need for that, really! I trust my eye for people, he's no charlatan — could it really be that the Crafting Bench is having an off-day?
There's a good chance of that — that being the Crafting Bench, I mean. You haven't been the only victims thus far.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Mr. Hampeq! Thanks for your help earlier.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: No sweat. Treating those who are injured is one of my duties. Regarding the Crafting Bench, have you ever heard about the "Locusts"?

choices.text: First time for me.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: It's fine if you've never heard of them. We logistics people have never really cared about being praised or being recognized like the true warriors. As far as we're concerned, ours is still honorable work.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: In the past, the Hawkwings — the faction I belong to — has always been in charge of the Stadium's various facilities. Rule-abiding sorts, we are, always doing our best to do our part.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: But we've not had many new members join in recent years... We've got experience on our side, but even the best can't be everywhere at once when there's so much to do. Can't say we've made no mistakes, either.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Eventually, after taking the opinions of various parties into account, the Speaker's Chamber ruled that we should regularly hold a tournament in which all factions could participate. The winners would earn the right to carry about our noble work.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: We were, unfortunately, beaten, and have temporarily lost that honor. Our successors were the Locusts. They run the show quite differently...

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: If they'd gone and given the work their all, I'd have no gripes. But — and I'm putting this as generously as possible — I've never seen a bunch of louts as hellbent on profit as they are...

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: And in the latest tournament, we Hawkwings encountered an unusually high number of accidents, hamstringing our performance.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: And many were linked using alchemical potions, just like what happened to Sumac.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: I've been thinking that they've done... something... to the Crafting Bench. Before, they were just targeting us Hawkwings, but now others have gotten involved... They've gone way over the line!

choices.text: Umm, you say that, but...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've only just heard of these factions... It does sound like you've got some serious beef, but...

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Yeah. Without evidence, even the Speaker's Chamber has its hands tied.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: It's all my fault! If only I'd been more vigilant... The reason we missed out on collecting hard evidence before is because I never imagined they'd stoop to such low-down, no-good dirty tricks.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: I know this sounds crass, but thanks to Sumac's injury, we now have a chance to investigate this affair.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: You're an outsider, a third party to this whole conflict. With you as our witnesses, we'll be able to expose The Locusts' perfidy — not just for our sakes, but everyone's.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: I get where Mr. Hampeq's coming from. If the factions in charge of public amenities are up to no good, we're all in trouble.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: But my testimony alone won't cut it, will it? If we go back now and check out that Crafting Bench out...

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: It's already too late. The Locusts are a tricksy bunch. It won't be that easy to unmask them. To be honest, the fact that an outsider to our conflict was injured was... a happy accident.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Whatever the case, there's no doubt that any trace of tampering will have been scrubbed clean by the time we investigate the Crafting Bench.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Hmm... You seem intimately familiar with how the Locusts operate.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Of course. They're our rivals, the ones who stole our glory from us...

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: ...Anyway, since there's no tournament on today, I'm going to collect testimony from some previous victims. Would you two mind coming along?

choices.text: Oh boy! Is that drudgery I smell...?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: You'll be rewarded generously. This I guarantee.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess we just can't refuse requests for help, can we?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: You rest here first, Sumac. We'll meet up with you again once we have the evidence we need.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Alright. *sigh* Sorry for dragging you two into this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't say that! If you had to blame someone... then, uh, blame the Locusts! Yeah, so we're doing this for the good of everyone!

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: That's right. What we do, we do for the benefit of all, and it is a good thing indeed. Anyway, no time to lose. Let's go down to the outdoor training grounds and collect some testimony.

choices.text: A fair sum makes drudgery quite tolerable.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: And a fair sum you shall have.

choices.text: An utterly despicable pack of scoundrels!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You say that, but those are just guesses right now, aren't they?

choices.text: Oh yeah, sure, they're the whos in the where doing the whatsits, yeah?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't act like you're in the know when you obviously don't have a clue!

choices.text: Poison isn't exactly a common cold.

talks.objective: Go to the outdoor training area to collect testimony

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Found you at last, Anela. Would you reconsider the matter I wrote to you about?

dialogues.speaker: Anela
dialogues.text: Stickier than a tick, you are, chasing me all the way here. Well? What's in it for me?

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: ...I mean, you are a member of the Hawkwings...

dialogues.speaker: Anela
dialogues.text: I "was." I may be a good swimmer, but that doesn't mean I'll stay onboard your sinking ship.

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Couldn't you at least provide some testimony?

dialogues.speaker: Anela
dialogues.text: And drop myself in the pot of trouble you're brewing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh, this feels like a waste of time. We should just go back and look for Sumac.

dialogues.speaker: Anela
dialogues.text: Oh? Well, well, who are these two little cuties? Help you hired, Hampeq?

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Y—You could say that.

dialogues.speaker: Anela
dialogues.text: #Good. I've changed my mind. Youngsters with potential are just my jam. How about this, {M#little lad}{F#young lass}? If you pass my test, I'll consider giving you a statement after all.

choices.text: Color me shocked and surprised — a test.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess they really are part of the same faction, huh?

response.speaker: Anela
response.text: Ah, very good! Shall we begin?

choices.text: Bring it on.
Let me make some preparations.

response.speaker: Anela
response.text: No rush, take your time.

choices.text: Gotta admit, I'm not feeling it right now...

response.speaker: Anela
response.text: And would a little... extra reward from yours truly sweeten the pot?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Please let us give it a go!

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Hey, Ogun, it's been a while. You still remember the Crafting Bench incident? Just wanted to hear what you have to say about that...

dialogues.speaker: Ogun
dialogues.text: Seriously? You're still hung up about that? What's the point?

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Don't you worry, I've got my ways.

dialogues.speaker: Ogun
dialogues.text: Is your way relying on outsiders to interfere?

choices.text: And here we see dissent in its natural habitat, slaying a cause so the foe need not.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Sorry. I know we're not making the best account of ourselves...

response.speaker: Ogun
response.text: Outsider you are, and outsider you remain. However...

response.speaker: Ogun
response.text: Pass my training. Prove yourself worthy of my trust. Ask again after that, and you'll get your answers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, aren't we here to get testimonies? How did this turn into a test of strength?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Sorry, can't help you there. We Hawkwings have traditionally prized strength above all else, and Ogun's an archconservative even by our conservative standards...

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Better to just take his challenge rather than waste your breath. I have faith in your abilities.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay then...

response.speaker: Ogun
response.text: Done thinking it over? Ready to accept my challenge?

choices.text: Bring it on.
I'll need a moment to prepare.

response.speaker: Ogun
response.text: See to it, and then come to me.

choices.text: Could you consider me "elite reinforcements" instead?

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: So you're here just to gloat and revel in the humiliation of a defeated opponent? That's not a hobby I'd flaunt.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back, Sumac. Sorry to keep you waiting!

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Hey there! You were gone a pretty long time, to be honest. Did the testimony gathering not go so well?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... The Hawkwings have some really weird rules. We had to pass tests before they'd talk to us! And the reasons they gave were all over the place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we got a certificate for every test we passed, Paimon would totally be a Master already!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, we're definitely due for a title upgrade.

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Haha, I see. Shame I wasn't there to see everything go down, then! Bet I'd have become a skilled fighter in my own right by now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're passionate about martial training, aren't you? Still, Paimon's not sure the Hawkwings' methods would be for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, Hampeq, it seems like you aren't exactly everyone's favorite fellow. Weren't you all companions once?

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Huh? Sorry, did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, they're... kinda detached? Like they don't care about what you're doing? Or maybe they don't approve?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's so strange. Isn't exposing wrongdoing and punishing perpetrators the right thing to do? So why would they act like that...?

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: I'm afraid that the Hawkwings' being scattered like so many grains of sand is a disgrace I must bear responsibility for as one of its members.

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Still, I hope that this is our chance to reunite — I'll do anything to regain our honor.

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: I mean, don't they say that the truth oft winds up in the custody of the few? I won't throw in the towel just because I'm in the minority.

choices.text: I've heard that one before.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Well, the truth will be revealed soon, won't it? The Speaker's Chamber will judge based on the evidence both parties provide, so please, I'd like to ask you to be present as witnesses.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Hmm... Are you sure my testimony would be valid? Maybe I just had an accident that was totally unrelated to the Locusts.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, couldn't you just get Sumac to take the stand? What would we be there for?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: No, all of your testimony is absolutely necessary. Don't worry, I won't ask you to act against your convictions or involve you in anything unjust. Just tell the truth — that'll do.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Hmm... Well, you did help me when I was injured earlier, Mr. Hampeq, so I owe you that much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Is it really necessary? Oh well... We might as well help get to the bottom of this, huh, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Thank you all! In that case, let us meet at the outside training grounds in two days.

choices.text: You could always be in the minority because you're mistaken, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Pampa, we're here about...

dialogues.speaker: Pampa
dialogues.text: Oh, I've been waiting. Heard you all just fine, and reckoned I'd be next — just didn't expect to sit through one of Ogun's old-grumbler lectures first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice! That saves us the trouble of explaining. You can start anytime — we'll write it all down!

dialogues.speaker: Pampa
dialogues.text: Oh, no need to be hasty... "Pass my training. Prove yourself worthy of trust. Ask again after that, and you'll get your answers."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This again? Why!?

dialogues.speaker: Pampa
dialogues.text: Don't you think you learn a lot just by watching others overcome obstacles? And if you don't think so, I sure do.

dialogues.speaker: Pampa
dialogues.text: As such, I too would like a chance to learn from you, in return for my testimony. Can't let Ogun monopolize all the fun like that, now can we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Is that how this works?

dialogues.speaker: Pampa
dialogues.text: Of course. Why wouldn't it be? And if you're willing, let's start now!

choices.text: The sooner the better.
One moment. Let me prep.

response.speaker: Pampa
response.text: Of course. Making a mistake because you're in bad form would suck.

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: Tlalepa! Tlalepa! Bad news!

dialogues.speaker: Tlalepa
dialogues.text: *yawn* Seriously? What're you yelling about? Disturbed my beauty sleep, you did.

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: Someone's exposed us! I was able to smooth it over for the time being, but...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Wait a minute, we've got two Tozans here!)

choices.text: (Twins. As I thought.)

response.speaker: Tlalepa
response.text: Seriously, bro? Did you invite those two "guests" over as well? And are they here to get pranked, or are you pranking me?

response.speaker: Tozan
response.text: It's you two...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: To think you two set up shop right under the noses of everyone who goes to the Stadium and didn't get discovered! Is this what they call "hiding in plain sight"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You two... Uh, pieces of evidence! We already know your secret. Come with us to the Speaker's Chamber, and let us hear the truth!

response.speaker: Tlalepa
response.text: Well, I'll have to request that you keep our little secret. Big Bro, you're the one who brought this on us, so you're going to owe me.

response.speaker: Tozan
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Keep your secret? We're on the side of truth here! We're not that easy to bribe...

response.speaker: Tlalepa
response.text: Don't get ahead of yourself — Who said anything about a bribe? There's only one way you can be sure a secret's kept.

choices.text: (Wow, they do look exactly the same!)

dialogues.speaker: Pampa
dialogues.text: Amazing. Simply amazing!

choices.text: Did you get all that? There'll be a test later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, were you really trying to teach him? We're here to collect testimonies, you know!

response.speaker: Pampa
response.text: 'Course we can, I'm a man of my word. I'll tell you all I know.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Pampa vividly recounts the mishap he encountered before, which Hampeq records in a more concise form.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Thank you for your testimony. With this, we're one solid step closer to reclaiming the honor that is rightfully ours.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? He sure did a great job telling the story, but as for how useful it'll be...

response.speaker: Pampa
response.text: Hey now, that's where you're a mistaken lil' miss. Form is about decorum, and decorum is crucial, you hear? Crucial! But in case you've never heard, stay a while, and listen...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Err... Can we just go now?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Then it's time we went to find Anela. She should be with the People of the Springs at this time. But before that...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You follow Hampeq to a secluded spot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's with all the mystery?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Well, this friend is... special. Sorry for the wait, Tozan. About that thing we agreed on earlier...

response.speaker: Tozan
response.text: Well, I'm here now, aren't I? Sure was a pain in the neck to squirrel these things out under the noses of my factionmates, though.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: My thanks. I'm afraid we'll have need of you in the future, too.

response.speaker: Tozan
response.text: Aw, come on! This is for everyone's benefit, isn't it?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Yes, indeed it is. You're a good fellow, worthy of respect. Until you showed up, I'd never have thought that a Locust would go against their own faction's interests...

response.speaker: Tozan
response.text: Ah, to be honest, it breaks my heart to know that some of us have sunk to such contemptible conduct.

response.speaker: Tozan
response.text: And yet, as a Locust, it'd be difficult for me to change the status quo, so some external help is quite welcome indeed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so you're helping the Hawkwings on the sly, then? W—Wouldn't that make you a traitor?

response.speaker: Tozan
response.text: Ah! Why put it in such harsh terms? Are our goals not aligned — to expose evildoers and see them punished?

response.speaker: Tozan
response.text: Well then. The hour grows late, so I'll be taking my leave. If you need anything else, just contact me. Good luck to you.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tozan leaves without a sound...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, what he gave you was...

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Intel on The Locusts, of course. It will buttress our testimony all the more. Honestly, I'm glad to know that reasonable people like Tozan still exist in that swarm of locusts.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Alright, let's keep gathering evidence. We can't let his goodwill go to waste. We'll find Anela over with the People of the Springs.

choices.text: We can get down to business now, right?

talks.objective: Go to the People of the Springs to meet Anela

dialogues.speaker: Wooden Crate
dialogues.text: A—achoo!

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Has the mood changed? I feel like I'm getting nervous, too...

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Haha, I didn't think I'd get beaten as soon as I arrived at the Stadium. This story's going to be a riot for my friends back home.

choices.text: Being the butt of a joke amongst friends is worth it sometimes.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: I think so too! My friends call it a kind of "unhealthy masochism," though... But I don't think my health has been negatively affected, so I'm probably fine.

choices.text: Must be saddening to have your friends laugh at you.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: You think so? I don't think they mean any harm. It was a pretty funny scene at any rate — I wouldn't mind if you laughed too.

dialogues.speaker: Anela
dialogues.text: #You're quite the budding talent, for sure. Y'know what? Forget Hampeq — why don't you join up with me instead, {M#lad}{F#lass}?

choices.text: Sounds good. Let's talk terms and compensation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's get back on topic, shall we? We're here to get her testimony, y'know.

response.speaker: Anela
response.text: That how it is? Shame. But I did agree, so...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Anela lazily relates her unpleasant encounter, while Hampeq pens it down faithfully in its entirety.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: That should be all our testimonies squared away... Are you really not coming back, Anela? Should we succeed this time...

response.speaker: Anela
response.text: You can invite me after the fact. You should know I can't stand men who are clingy despite being total failures — or do you?

response.speaker: Anela
response.text: Of course, you kids are a different story — my door's always open to you. And if you'd rather take this to a hot spring...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Err, w—we're busy right now! Byeee!

choices.text: No thanks. I've still got a ton of commissions on my docket...

talks.objective: Return to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Much obliged, then.

talks.objective: Go to the outdoor training area after two days

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: I'll leave submitting the victims' testimonies to you.

talks.objective: Go to the outdoor training area

dialogues.speaker: Pampa
dialogues.text: You ready? It is better to be patient at times like this... You can take your time, I'm in no hurry!

choices.text: Let's begin.
Wait a moment.

response.speaker: Pampa
response.text: Don't worry, I'm super patient!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, that's quite the crowd! Paimon's getting a bit nervous...

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: #Hey there, {NICKNAME}, Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sumac! There you are. How are you feeling?

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Great, thanks to you! Actually, I ended up going to other Crafting Benches to try that potion...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wow, you've got guts.

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: And it seems like the formula's fine — so yeah, told you I've got a good eye. The problem must've been with the Crafting Bench, then.

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Ah, look, we should be starting soon. See that person in the middle? That's Mr. Tenehua, the judge sent by the Speaker's Chamber.

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: The people facing Mr. Hampeq should be Locust members... Only two of them? That's fewer people than we have!

choices.text: (Huh, he looks familiar...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Ohh, right, so he really was a Locust. But wait, why's he standing on that side...?)

response.speaker: Tenehua
response.text: Ahem. It's about time, so let us get started. I'm sure that all present are well aware of this dispute, so I shall cut to the chase.

response.speaker: Tenehua
response.text: State your case, Hampeq.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: My thanks for the chance to speak. Everyone knows that the Locusts have replaced us Hawkwings for some time now. Yet, such grudges will not simply vanish.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: I'm sure it also goes without saying that we are still capable competitors. If we emerged victorious in another tournament, we would reclaim the glory that was once ours.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: But it just so happened that, on the eve of the event, our various contestants met with mishap after mishap... And each victim shared something in common: Their accident happened after using a Locust-managed Crafting Bench.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: I don't imagine it's a stretch to conclude that the Locusts were the sole beneficiaries of the resultant injuries. As such, we can see that they had both the motive and the ability to put such a plan into practice...

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: Just one minute there, bro, I'm going to ask you to slow your roll. Motives and capabilities are one thing, but doing it is a whole different ball game.

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: Also, let's be real, you're not the only ones who have beef with us. You know how it is. "When you've got 99 problems, what's a couple mo'?"

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: You think we've got the time to go around exacting revenge, one by one... And besides, I haven't heard of too many people getting injured after using Crafting Benches lately. You sure it's not just your persecution complex acting up?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: There haven't been many cases "lately," but they happened, didn't they? And the fact that such targeted attacks stopped happening just as I started investigating is quite unnatural, don't you think?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Moreover, there was a recent victim — someone completely uninvolved in this conflict, in fact.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Sumac, that young lady over there, suddenly felt unwell after ingesting a potion crafted using one of your Crafting Benches just a few days ago. She had to be carried back to the Stadium for treatment.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: #The outlander travelers {NICKNAME} and Paimon can corroborate her testimony, and the two of them were also present when I collected testimonies from the Hawkwing victims.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Mr. Hampeq speaks the truth. I did verify if the formula was suitable afterward. I can only conclude that the Crafting Bench itself was faulty somehow...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, and speaking of what happened that day, we didn't use that Crafting Bench in the first place because it seemed weird.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: #Here also are the victim testimonies, good judge, that I gathered together with {NICKNAME} and Paimon. If you would, you two?

choices.text: Side? I don't remember joining the Hawkwings.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: That's true... Well, be that as it may, you could still say that we're on the side of truth, right?

talks.objective: Submit the victims' testimonies to the judge

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: Pass the Hawkwings victim testimonies to me once you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: Well, it certainly appears that this is no groundless accusation after all. Any objections, Itzcuin?

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: Alright, so, let's just say that the Crafting Bench we're responsible for has malfunctioned. That, at most, amounts to... what, negligent management?

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: I mean, not like we hogged all the glory for ages like the Hawkwings, so we're a bit lacking in experience. Some mistakes are bound to happen. Gotta give us newbies a chance, right?

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: As for our forerunners, we've got nothing but respect for 'em — But accusing us of sabotaging them? Now that's just too much!

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: How about this? We'll actively discuss compensation with those who suffered losses due to our oversight. Will that do?

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Don't think I'm blind to the strawman you're propping up! You clearly deliberately targeted us Hawkwings. There's no way this was unintentional or the result of some kinda negligence!

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: And do you have proof of malicious intent? Don't think you can get that from the victim testimonies.

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Of course I do! In fact, I've got intel from within your little gang!

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: See the Loach Pearls on this invoice? The timing of the Locusts' mass purchase of them coincides exactly with that of the Hawkwings' mishaps.

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Now, we all know that Loach Pearls are not materials that need to be stockpiled in large amounts, and similar substances were found in the potions imbibed by the victims.

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: ...Where did you get that invoice?

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: From a member of your corrupt organization whose conscience hasn't yet breathed its last, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Judging by his reaction, that sure hit him where it hurts!)

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: #For safety reasons, I will not disclose this stout-hearted person's name. But I guarantee that {NICKNAME} and Paimon were there when I received the invoice, and they can corroborate the event.

choices.text: We were indeed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, they even said it broke their heart to witness such contemptible conduct by other Locusts...

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: Really? And here I thought we were famous for being earnest dullards. Didn't know we had someone that eloquent on staff. I'd really like to meet 'em.

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: Hmph. Anyway, let's just assume the list in your hands is genuine. So what? It's circumstantial evidence — your accusation remains mere speculation.

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: This invoice could just as well point to some rotten, traitorous Locusts using our operating funds to buy the Loach Pearls so they can build an artificial hot spring in their backyard.

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: And wouldn't that be a terrible disgrace for us? Don't worry, I promise we'll investigate thoroughly, and then give a full accounting to everyone. How's that?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: How unsightly. Are you really going to just deny everything to the bitter end?

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: More like your evidence just doesn't cut it.

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: How about this, then? This picture clearly shows someone tampering with the Crafting Bench, with a chest full of Loach Pearls next to them!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, that person sure looks familiar... Isn't that you, Sumac?

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Ah, so it is!

choices.text: What a coincidence...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure is!

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: Didn't expect such a move from you, to be sure... But please, everyone, think for a second. Is this stuff actually proving his claims, or is it simply more of the same old circumstantial evidence?

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: Even if this picture could prove that someone tampered with the Bench, can you prove that person to be a Locust?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: And if I said that this picture was given to me by a Locust, just like that invoice?

response.speaker: Tenehua
response.text: #Well, then. Would you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, be able to vouch for that?

choices.text: No, I don't remember that happening...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is the first time we're seeing this picture, and judging by your reaction, Sumac, this is your first time as well, right?

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Nope, never. Sorry, Mr. Hampeq, but we can't give false testimony.

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: So, does this "stout-hearted" person you speak of truly exist? Or did you conspire with those fellows over there to invent this story out of whole cloth?

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: We're a united lot, we Locusts — is that not how we overcame you scattered Hawkwings? I find it... difficult to imagine that we'd have a turncoat amongst us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #We take on almost any request, but we've got principles, too! We wouldn't lie at a time like this, right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Tenehua
response.text: Hmm... Though it does seem that the Locusts are not above suspicion, this is not enough to make a final judgment.

response.speaker: Tenehua
response.text: If your "stout-hearted" special friend could testify in person, Hampeq, that would make things much simpler! But you claim that there's no such person, yes, Itzcuin?

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: Absolutely. There's no way a traitor exists among our ranks.

response.speaker: Tenehua
response.text: Well, since this has reached an impasse, there's no point in continuing. Unless you have something to add, Hampeq, let's call it for today.

response.speaker: Tenehua
response.text: Still, before we adjourn, please submit the evidence you just presented.

choices.text: I cannot.
Are you some sort of important figure, to be under surveillance like that?

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Huh? Would someone as ordinary as me really need monitoring?

choices.text: We did indeed encounter a "special friend."

talks.objective: Submit the purchase invoice to the judge

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: You'll have to submit... the Locusts' Purchase Invoice. Ready?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Looks like this is the end of the line, Hampeq.

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: N—No, we still... We can still... Mr. Tenehua, I'd like to identify the Locust member who provided me with the intel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh!? W—Wait a minute... That's not a good idea, is it!?

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: But before that, I hope that the Speaker's Chamber can extend protection to the person I'm going to identify. That will be no problem, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: We can consider it. This Crafting Bench affair is an affair neither big nor small, but the Speaker's Chamber nonetheless hopes for a straightforward end to the dispute.

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: If both sides agree to this, I assure you that we will not allow any acts of retaliation from the Locusts.

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Of course he'd agree. He said it himself, that our goals were aligned — to expose evildoers and see them punished.

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: In fact, I believe that he came here today precisely because he agrees. Isn't that right, Tozan?

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: Y'hear that? He named you the traitor.

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: Well, that's trouble. I've got no idea what you're talking about, Mr. Hampeq. I know you're in a hurry to find some way out, but you've got the wrong guy.

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: What? What's wrong with you? Didn't you give me the Crafting Bench picture yourself? That facility is managed by the Locusts, so only you could have taken that photo...

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: Well, that's just the thing. I checked that photo, and the Crafting Bench in it isn't one under our management.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, Paimon's getting lost already. We first met Sumac at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, didn't we? So that Bench must've been the one there, right?

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Exactly, I remember it clearly. That was my first time at the Stadium, and I was happy to make good friends, only to meet misfortune not long after.

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: So, can we take that to mean that the Crafting Bench was a fake, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A fake Crafting Bench? How can that be?

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: Well, if people can fabricate evidence, is a fake Crafting Bench that unbelievable? You know, other than the question of motive—

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: I mean, it's not like someone would pour effort into a fake Crafting Bench with which to frame us Locusts, not caring if they injured an innocent passerby in the course of fabricating their evidence...

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: ...Before attempting to use scummy tricks to try and create internal strife between us?

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: #B—But what about the invoice? {NICKNAME} and Paimon were both there when you handed it to me on the tournament rest day. They can vouch for me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Let's not think too hard about Tozan's change in attitude first. Let's just tell the truth.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We did indeed see him.

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: Wait, you mean the day we had no tournament on? Well, that's weird, because, dear judge Mr. Tenehua, I clearly recall we were soaking in a hot spring on the People of the Springs' turf that very same day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? But we saw him, and so close to this place, too...

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: Hey, hey, now that's crazy talk if I've ever heard it. How can one person be in two places at once? But I had to take a guess based on a certain someone's nature, the one you saw might've been a fake.

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: I mean, with the Crafting Bench a fake and the witness a bust... Are we sure we can trust the invoice? Are we sure it's not all nonsense?

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: I'm sure everyone here can figure it out — this is all a frame-up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...A frame-up?

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: #That's right. Whether the Crafting Bench, the injured Sumac, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, who were roped in as witnesses... You orchestrated all this yourself, didn't you, Hampeq?

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: You know that the scattered Hawkwings weren't any match for us. That's why you had to resort to dirty tricks.

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: Shame, though. You were destined to fail the moment you decided to forge evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: Lies will always be exposed. And now, everyone will look upon your every word with suspicion. It won't matter what evidence you present...

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: "Will it be a fake, just like before?" That's what everyone won't be able to help but think!

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: There's no credibility left in the Hawkwings, and you're the one to blame — serves you right, thinking that you could indulge your selfish desires under the guise of "justice."

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: Nothing to say, then? *sigh* This has proved more complicated than I anticipated. I'm afraid my judgment will have to wait for another day.

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you were deceived into giving false testimony, so I shall not press charges against you this time.

choices.text: But my eyes didn't deceive me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. Paimon was there too! We saw it with our own eyes, and even talked to him! It was him for sure!

response.speaker: Tenehua
response.text: So you mean to call me, the judge, a liar?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we're not saying that! Hmm... H—Hey, say something, Hampeq... Or was the Tozan we met that day an impostor you put up to the job?

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: Impossible. That was the Tozan I know. And he did give me the Crafting Bench picture... I've been had! I don't know how he did it, though...

response.speaker: Hampeq
response.text: And the situation is as he says... I could not explain the most crucial mystery, and now, my every word arouses suspicion! ...I've already utterly lost!

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Hey, chin up, Mr. Hampeq! We warriors of Natlan don't throw in the towel that easily. Like I said, I've got a good eye for people... I know you're not lying.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Itzcuin was confident when he spoke, and didn't seem like one to purposely lie. But Tozan... Now that's an experienced liar.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But from what happened just now, everyone must've been convinced that Hampeq was the architect of all this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, Paimon doesn't know who to trust anymore... Now she's even doubting your words, Sumac! I—Is this what they call a "crisis of confidence"?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: At times like these, a little out-of-the-box thinking is needed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Out of the box? How?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's not that Hampeq intended this as a frame-up from the start.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Rather, Tozan saw all this coming, and struck first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Huh?

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: So you mean that, suspecting that Mr. Hampeq's investigation might turn up something for real and actually hurt the Locusts...

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: ...Tozan pretended to help, only to lure him into making the wrong decisions so he could use the case to destroy the Hawkwings' credibility?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... That's definitely possible!

response.speaker: Itzcuin
response.text: Hello? This thing's over! A done deal! Seriously, this is getting more ludicrous by the moment. What idiocy are you gonna spew next? Going to say we Locusts bought out the judge and had him commit perjury?

response.speaker: Tenehua
response.text: I know you don't doubt your eyes, but neither do I.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Hmm... I doubt Mr. Tenehua's lying. There's only one possibility left, which is that you all saw Tozan on the same day, but in different places.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But a person can't be in two places at once, can they...?

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Well, just like with the Crafting Bench where we first met, Paimon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There were likely two Crafting Benches at the Stadium then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Two Benches? So you mean that the real one was still in its original spot, and we just encountered a fake, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Though you say it was fake... But it wasn't much different from the real deal. If it hadn't been tampered with, it would've functioned normally.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Exactly, so both Crafting Benches were genuine.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just like there is no fake Tozan — instead, there are two of him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Two... Tozans...? OH! Paimon knows where you going with this!

response.speaker: Tenehua
response.text: Haha, well, if I hadn't known the man himself for so long, I might have seriously considered your hypothesis... Actually, maybe I should give it some thought, hmm?

response.speaker: Tozan
response.text: ...I'm afraid this nonsense is not worth wasting your precious time on, sir.

response.speaker: Tenehua
response.text: Oh, come on, Tozan, I was just joking. No need to be so nervous! Anyway, we're done for today. Hampeq, Itzcuin, you stay for a bit. I'll need you to come with me to the Speaker's Chamber...

response.speaker: Tenehua
response.text: And as for the rest of you, you're free to go.

response.speaker: Tozan
response.text: I've got other things to do. See you.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tozan leaves in silence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* For a moment there, Paimon thought we'd be able to, y'know...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shazam! Turn things around at the last second, an epic climax!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But guess not. Not that we could provide anything more than guesses, though... What we really needed was two Tozans, right in front of us!

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Hmm... You know, we might actually have a chance at that. Have you heard the story of the foolish thief, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The foolish thief...? C'mon, don't keep Paimon on tenterhooks, just tell the story!

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: Alright, alright. Relax. So there was once a foolish thief who stole a gem from someone, and hid it in a place only he knew of.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: The owner of the gem only knew who it was who had committed the theft, not where the gem was hidden. But he was a smart man, and so he said to the thief...

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: "Hey, you! Thief! I know you stole my gem, so I've nicked it right back. Don't believe me? Go see for yourself!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #The owner's smart, so that's gotta be {NICKNAME} and Paimon. That makes the thief and the gem...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ah! Paimon's got it, for sure this time! C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's catch up with Tozan. He'll bring us right to his "gem" hidey-hole!

choices.text: I'm many things, but not a perjurer.

dialogues.speaker: Anela
dialogues.text: #Ready for the test, {M#lad}{F#lass}?

choices.text: Bring it on.
Hold on...

response.speaker: Anela
response.text: Hehe, sure, no problem.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You lock the two of them in the cages for now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph. You two were small time!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm honestly more curious...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...What made you think two-on-one would be fair odds — for you, I mean?

dialogues.speaker: Tlalepa
dialogues.text: You... You little brat! You're not what you seem at all! ...Two fists against four is unfair, but you alone count for eight at least!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfft. Don't be silly. Paimon counts four fists on your team, and four on ours. Fair's fair, and you lost square!

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: Alright. You win this round. But what about it? Sure, I pulled a trick or two... Does that mean Hampeq's a saint?

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: You all saw how dumbstruck he was. Everyone did. The Hawkwings' credibility's completely bust. Nothing you do will change that.

dialogues.speaker: Tozan
dialogues.text: I've already won! Reveal my secrets to the Chamber all you want. You won't save the Hawkwings...

choices.text: That's not for me to decide.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. We're on the side of the truth, nothing more, nothing less! Judging your dispute is up to the Speaker's Chamber.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We should be fine leaving them here for a bit, right? We've gotta hoof it back to the Stadium and tell Tenehua...

choices.text: I've no interest in your grievances.

talks.objective: Go to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame and report to the judge

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tenehua! Good thing you're still here...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell him the whole tale...

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: I've known Tozan for ages. Before he joined the Locusts, even... I've never heard he had a twin brother...

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: Could it be that he and this Tlalepa been switching places all this time, and we just didn't notice...?

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: It's quite hard to believe... But I doubt you'd joke about something like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you won't be laughing when you get to their hiding place. In fact, you'll be shocked! It's definitely much closer than you think!

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: Indeed, this is something I must personally verify. And if that's the case, some old cases will require reinvestigating... I'll be busy in the coming days, I expect.

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, thank you both very much.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, don't worry, we just don't like scammers... Speaking of which, Sumac helped a lot this time, didn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: Indeed, and I will remember it. Once the dust settles, I'll ensure that she is rewarded.

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: Now, I'd love to stay and chat, but as I have important matters at hand, please excuse me.

dialogues.speaker: Tenehua
dialogues.text: Again, thank you, and I hope things go well with you.

dialogues.speaker: Ogun
dialogues.text: As for today's training... Yes, that should do it.

choices.text: What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Ogun
response.text: I'm a coach. Other than developing training regimens, I don't have much else to do.

choices.text: Sorry to bother you.

response.speaker: Ogun
response.text: Mm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Well, are you ready?

choices.text: Bring it on.

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: I was waiting for you to say that.

choices.text: Hold on...

response.speaker: Sumac
response.text: No worries.

dialogues.speaker: Ogun
dialogues.text: Ready?

choices.text: Let's begin.
Wait a moment.

response.speaker: Ogun
response.text: Will do.

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm counting on you two.

dialogues.speaker: Pampa
dialogues.text: Is it worth getting that angry over? Honestly...

choices.text: What's wrong?

response.speaker: Pampa
response.text: *sigh* You'll really listen? That means a lot. Our little group broke up, you know? And it'd actually been a while, but then suddenly an old friend came knocking...

response.speaker: Pampa
response.text: Why else would someone suddenly connect out of the blue, unless they needed to borrow some money? Anyway, since we were once pretty tight buds, I gotta lend him at least a little, yeah? But oh no, this guy, not only did he not say thanks, he even told me off for not giving him enough!

response.speaker: Pampa
response.text: He even said something about how after the Hawkwings won back their rightful place he'd give me back double, blah blah.... *sigh* Not sure if he's just pigheaded or... Anyway, I'm an adult and generous to boot, so I decided to help as much as I could.

response.speaker: Pampa
response.text: I practically wanna give myself a medal!

choices.text: Sorry for disturbing you.

response.speaker: Pampa
response.text: Huh? Leaving already, just like that? Alrighty, then...

dialogues.speaker: Tlalepa
dialogues.text: Let me out of here and fight us again if you dare! You hear me!?

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: What's the Hawkwings' little helper looking for me for? I've got nothin' to say to the likes of you.

dialogues.speaker: Sumac
dialogues.text: Well, feels like things are getting weirder and weirder...

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: It's fine, there's still a way...

dialogues.speaker: Itzcuin
dialogues.text: If you've got other tricks up your sleeve, by all means, don't hold back. Hit me with everything you've got.

dialogues.speaker: Ogun
dialogues.text: I'm not too concerned about the outcome. This just happens to be my duty.

dialogues.speaker: Pampa
dialogues.text: Have I arrived too early? Are we not at the exciting bit yet? Or was there not one?

dialogues.speaker: Anela
dialogues.text: So many familiar faces... I can barely breathe. *sigh* The sooner this is over, the better.

dialogues.speaker: Ogun
dialogues.text: Hmph, just as I thought.

dialogues.speaker: Pampa
dialogues.text: Wait, could it be...?

dialogues.speaker: Anela
dialogues.text: This should be over soon, right? Phew... Now we can finally go back.

dialogues.speaker: Ogun
dialogues.text: Why don't you try it out before you give up?

dialogues.speaker: Pampa
dialogues.text: It's not over yet, is it? I'm keeping track of the time.

dialogues.speaker: Anela
dialogues.text: Giving up halfway ain't a good habit. Sure you don't wanna hang in there a bit?

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Thanks for your hard work.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You take Sumac back to the Stadium and have her properly treated...

dialogues.speaker: Hampeq
dialogues.text: Let's go find Pampa next. It's not far from here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that we've gathered all the testimonies, shouldn't we go back to the Stadium and look for Sumac?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, we're back near the Stadium of the Sacred Flame again? Gah, he's so quick! We only lost sight for a second, and now he's gone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Good thing he left footprints, though! Let's follow his tracks, {NICKNAME}!
